security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel S-mode trap handler sets sstatus.SDT=1 (double-trap protection) then executes SRET to U/VS/VU, implicitly assuming the hardware will clear SDT — but either (a) the kernel is returning via SRET from S-mode, which is not covered by the spec's clearing rule (only SRET-in-M-mode clears MDT/SDT), or (b) Ssdbltrp is not implemented so SDT is never auto-cleared, or (c) the kernel returns via a path that does not go through M-mode MRET/SRET (e.g., direct S-mode SRET), leaving SDT stuck at 1 and causing the next S-mode trap to be treated as an unexpected double trap.
security_spec.summary: PR clarifies SRET-in-M-mode (not S-mode) clears MDT/SDT and SDT-clearing is gated on Ssdbltrp; kernel returning to userspace via S-mode SRET must explicitly clear SDT or risk trapping all subsequent S-mode exceptions as unexpected double-traps
